newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Radio reports Algerian GIA denying its leader killed.
newsitem.headline: Radio reports Algerian GIA denying its leader killed.

text.p: The Armed Islamic Group (GIA) has denied that its leader Antar Zouabri had been killed in an ambush in Algeria this week, a Moroccan radio said on Friday.
Medi-1, broadcasting from the north Moroccan city of Tangier, said it had received a statement from the GIA denying reports that Zouabri had been killed by Algerian security forces.
"The allegation concerning the Attatba operation and Zouabri's death are merely inventions devoid of any foundation," the radio quoted the statement as saying.
The statement carried the stamp of the GIA and the name of Zouabri, the radio said.
The radio said it could not authenticate the contents of the statement.
Algerian newspapers this week have reported a massive military operation in the Attatba area, between Tipaza and Blida, south of Algiers, in which up to 140 Moslem rebels have been reported killed.
Algerian news reports said Zouabri was among those killed while others said he was still trapped by besieging military forces.
There has been no official comment by Algeria on either the operation or the reports of rebel deaths.
